title: Squanto Teaches the Pilgrims to Plant
text:
Tisquantum, known to the English as Squanto, came from the Patuxet people on the coast of what is now Massachusetts. In 1614 an English captain, Thomas Hunt, kidnapped him and other men and sold them as slaves in Spain. Squanto escaped to England, learned English, and finally returned home in 1619 only to find his whole village dead from an epidemic.

In the winter of 1620 to 1621 the Pilgrims settled on that same empty site and named it Plymouth. About half of them died before spring. In March 1621 a Native man named Samoset walked into the settlement, and soon after brought Squanto, who could speak to them in their own language.

William Bradford, the colony's governor, describes what followed in Of Plymouth Plantation. Squanto helped arrange a peace treaty with Massasoit, leader of the Wampanoag. He showed the colonists how to plant corn with fish to fertilize it, where to catch fish and how to find other food, and he guided and interpreted for them. Bradford called him a special instrument sent by God for their good. Squanto's own position was complicated, and he also used his role to build influence for himself. He died of a fever in 1622.
lesson: Help can come from the person you least expect, even one with every reason to resent you. Be open to it, and remember who carried you through your first hard season.
source: William Bradford, Of Plymouth Plantation, Book 2, years 1621 and 1622
